sanskrit: tatra mallā naṭā jhallāḥ sūtā vaitālikās tathā upatasthur mahātmānaṃ saptarātraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: There wrestlers, actors, jesters, bards, and panegyrists attended the great-souled Yudhiṣṭhira for seven nights.

sanskrit: tathā sa kṛtvā pūjāṃ tāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaḥ tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ ramyāyāṃ reme śakro yathā divi
english: Having thus performed that ceremony of honor, the Pāṇḍava together with his brothers took delight in that beautiful assembly hall, as Indra rejoices in heaven.

sanskrit: sabhāyām ṛṣayas tasyāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha āsate āsāṃ cakrur narendrāś ca nānādeśasamāgatāḥ
english: Sages were seated in that assembly hall together with the Pāṇḍavas, and kings who had come from many different lands also took their seats there.

sanskrit: asito devalaḥ satyaḥ sarpamālī mahāśirāḥ arvāvasuḥ sumitraś ca maitreyaḥ śunako baliḥ
english: Asita, Devala, Satya, Sarpamali, Mahasiras, Arvāvasu, Sumitrā, Maitreya, Śunaka, and Bali were among them.

sanskrit: bako dālbhyaḥ sthūlaśirāḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ śukaḥ sumantur jaiminiḥ pailo vyāsaśiṣyās tathā vayam
english: Baka Dalbhya, Sthulasiras, Krishnadvapayana, Śuka, Sumantru, Jaimini, Paila — the disciples of Vyāsa — and ourselves were likewise present.

sanskrit: tittirir yājñavalkyaś ca sasuto lomaharṣaṇaḥ apsuhomyaś ca dhaumyaś ca āṇīmāṇḍavyakauśikau
english: Tittiri, Yājñavalkya with his son, Lomaharṣaṇa, Apsuhomya, Dhaumya, and also Animandavya and Kauśika were there.

sanskrit: dāmoṣṇīṣas traivaṇiś ca parṇādo ghaṭajānukaḥ mauñjāyano vāyubhakṣaḥ pārāśaryaś ca sārikau
english: Damoshniṣa, Traivaṇi, Parṇada, Ghaṭajanuka, Mauñjayana, Vayubhaksha, Parasharya, and the two known as Sarika were present.

sanskrit: balavākaḥ śinīvākaḥ sutyapālaḥ kṛtaśramaḥ jātūkarṇaḥ śikhāvāṃś ca subalaḥ pārijātakaḥ
english: Balavaka, Shinivaka, Sutyapala, Kṛtaśrama, Jatukarṇa, Shikhavant, Subala, and Parijataka were also there.

sanskrit: parvataś ca mahābhāgo mārkaṇḍeyas tathā muniḥ pavitrapāṇiḥ sāvarṇir bhālukir gālavas tathā
english: The greatly blessed Parvata, the sage Mārkaṇḍeya, Pavitrapani, Savarni, Bhāluki, and likewise Gālava were present.

sanskrit: jaṅghābandhuś ca raibhyaś ca kopavegaśravā bhṛguḥ haribabhruś ca kauṇḍinyo babhrumālī sanātanaḥ
english: Janghabandhu, Raibhya, Kopavegashrava, Bhṛgu, Haribabhru, Kaundinia, Babhrumali, and Sanatana were there as well.

sanskrit: kakṣīvān auśijaś caiva nāciketo 'tha gautamaḥ paiṅgo varāhaḥ śunakaḥ śāṇḍilyaś ca mahātapāḥ karkaro veṇujaṅghaś ca kalāpaḥ kaṭha eva ca
english: Kakṣīvān Auśija, Nāciketa, Gautama, Painga, Varaha, Śunaka, the great ascetic Śāṇḍilya, Karkara, Venujangha, Kalapa, and Katha were also among them.

sanskrit: munayo dharmasahitā dhṛtātmāno jitendriyāḥ ete cānye ca bahavo vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ
english: These sages, virtuous and righteous, of firm minds and with senses subdued, and many others well-versed in the Vedas and their auxiliary branches, were gathered there.

sanskrit: upāsate mahātmānaṃ sabhāyām ṛṣisattamāḥ kathayantaḥ kathāḥ puṇyā dharmajñāḥ śucayo 'malāḥ
english: The foremost of sages, knowing dharma, pure and spotless, attended upon the great-souled king in the assembly hall, narrating sacred stories.

sanskrit: tathaiva kṣatriyaśreṣṭhā dharmarājam upāsate śrīmān mahātmā dharmātmā muñjaketur vivardhanaḥ
english: Likewise the foremost of kshatriyas attended upon the king of dharma — the splendid, great-souled, dharma-minded Muñjaketu Vardhana.

sanskrit: saṃgrāmajid durmukhaś ca ugrasenaś ca vīryavān kakṣasenaḥ kṣitipatiḥ kṣemakaś cāparājitaḥ kāmbojarājaḥ kamalaḥ kampanaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Saṃgrāmajit, Durmukha, the mighty Ugrasena, Kakshena the lord of the earth, Kṣemaka the unconquered, the king of the Kāmbojas, Kamala, and the greatly powerful Kampana were present.

sanskrit: satataṃ kampayām āsa yavanān eka eva yaḥ yathāsurān kālakeyān devo vajradharas tathā
english: He alone had constantly shaken the Yavanas, just as the god who wields the thunderbolt shakes the Kalakeya demons.

sanskrit: jaṭāsuro madrakāntaś ca rājā; kuntiḥ kuṇindaś ca kirātarājaḥ tathāṅgavaṅgau saha puṇḍrakeṇa; pāṇḍyoḍrarājau saha cāndhrakeṇa
english: The king Jatasura and Madrakanta, Kuntī, Kuṇinda, the king of the Kirātas, the rulers of Aṅga and Vanga together with the king of Puṇḍra, and the kings of the Pandyas and Oḍras together with the king of the Andhras were there.

sanskrit: kirātarājaḥ sumanā yavanādhipatis tathā cāṇūro devarātaś ca bhojo bhīmarathaś ca yaḥ
english: The king of the Kirātas named Sumana, the lord of the Yavanas, Cāṇūra, Devarata, the Bhoja, and the one called Bhimaratha were there.

sanskrit: śrutāyudhaś ca kāliṅgo jayatsenaś ca māgadhaḥ suśarmā cekitānaś ca suratho 'mitrakarṣaṇaḥ
english: Śrutāyudha the Kaliṅga, Jayatsena the Magadha, Susharmana, Cekitāna, and Suratha the destroyer of foes were present.

sanskrit: ketumān vasudānaś ca vaideho 'tha kṛtakṣaṇaḥ sudharmā cāniruddhaś ca śrutāyuś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Ketuman, Vasudāna, the king of Videha, Kritakshana, Sudharmana, Aniruddha, and the mighty Śrutāyu were also there.

sanskrit: anūparājo durdharṣaḥ kṣemajic ca sudakṣiṇaḥ śiśupālaḥ sahasutaḥ karūṣādhipatis tathā
english: The invincible king of the Anūpa country, Kshemajit, Sudakṣiṇa, Śiśupāla with his hundred sons, and likewise the lord of the Karūṣas were present.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇīnāṃ caiva durdharṣāḥ kumārā devarūpiṇaḥ āhuko vipṛthuś caiva gadaḥ sāraṇa eva ca
english: The invincible princes of the Vṛṣṇis, god-like in appearance — Ahuka, Viprithu, Gada, and Sāraṇa — were also there.

sanskrit: akrūraḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātyakiś ca śineḥ sutaḥ bhīṣmako 'thāhṛtiś caiva dyumatsenaś ca vīryavān kekayāś ca maheṣvāsā yajñasenaś ca saumakiḥ
english: Akrura, Kṛtavarmā, Sātyaki the son of Śini, Bhīṣmaka, Ahriti, the mighty Dyumatsena, the great archers the Kekayas, and Yajñasena the son of Saumaka were present.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ cāpi saṃśritya rājaputrā mahābalāḥ aśikṣanta dhanurvedaṃ rauravājinavāsasaḥ
english: Taking refuge with Arjuna, mighty princes clad in deer and antelope hides learned the science of archery there.

sanskrit: tatraiva śikṣitā rājan kumārā vṛṣṇinandanāḥ raukmiṇeyaś ca sāmbaś ca yuyudhānaś ca sātyakiḥ
english: There too, O king, were trained the princes of the Vṛṣṇi clan — the son of Rukmiṇī, Samba, and Yuyudhāna the son of Sātyaki.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo rājānaḥ pṛthivīpate dhanaṃjayasakhā cātra nityam āste sma tumburuḥ
english: These and many other kings, O lord of the earth, were present there, and Tumburu, the friend of Dhanañjaya, also always abided there.

sanskrit: citrasenaḥ sahāmātyo gandharvāpsarasas tathā gītavāditrakuśalāḥ śamyātālaviśāradāḥ
english: Citrasena, accompanied by his ministers, and the Gandharvas and Apsaras, skilled in song and instrumental music, expert in rhythm and beat, were also present.

sanskrit: pramāṇe 'tha layasthāne kiṃnarāḥ kṛtaniśramāḥ saṃcoditās tumburuṇā gandharvāḥ sahitā jaguḥ
english: Kiṃnaras accomplished in proper measure and in the right tempo, urged on by Tumburu, sang together with the Gandharvas.

sanskrit: gāyanti divyatānais te yathānyāyaṃ manasvinaḥ pāṇḍuputrān ṛṣīṃś caiva ramayanta upāsate
english: Those noble beings sang with divine melodies according to proper rule, delighting and attending upon the sons of Pāṇḍu and the sages.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ sabhāyām āsīnāḥ suvratāḥ satyasaṃgarāḥ divīva devā brahmāṇaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram upāsate
english: Seated in that assembly hall, those of good vows and true resolve attended upon Yudhiṣṭhira as the gods in heaven attend upon Brahmā.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tatropaviṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu mahatsu copaviṣṭeṣu gandharveṣu ca bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were seated there, O Bhārata, and the great Gandharvas were likewise seated,

sanskrit: lokān anucaran sarvān āgamat tāṃ sabhām ṛṣiḥ nāradaḥ sumahātejā ṛṣibhiḥ sahitas tadā
english: The sage Nārada, of great brilliance, who roams through all the worlds, came to that assembly hall then, accompanied by sages.

sanskrit: pārijātena rājendra raivatena ca dhīmatā sumukhena ca saumyena devarṣir amitadyutiḥ sabhāsthān pāṇḍavān draṣṭuṃ prīyamāṇo manojavaḥ
english: The divine sage of boundless radiance came with Parijata, the wise Raivata, and the gentle Sumukha, moving swift as thought, joyfully desiring to see the Pāṇḍavas assembled in the hall, O king of kings.

sanskrit: tam āgatam ṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā nāradaṃ sarvadharmavit sahasā pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaḥ pratyutthāyānujaiḥ saha abhyavādayata prītyā vinayāvanatas tadā
english: Seeing the sage Nārada arrive, the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, who knew all dharma, quickly rose together with his younger brothers and greeted him with affection, bowing humbly at that time.

sanskrit: tadarham āsanaṃ tasmai saṃpradāya yathāvidhi arcayām āsa ratnaiś ca sarvakāmaiś ca dharmavit
english: Offering him a seat worthy of him according to proper rites, the one who knew dharma honored him with jewels and with all things desired.

sanskrit: so 'rcitaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sarvair maharṣir vedapāragaḥ dharmakāmārthasaṃyuktaṃ papracchedaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Honored by all the Pāṇḍavas, the great sage who had mastered the Vedas then questioned Yudhiṣṭhira on matters combining dharma, desire, and material welfare.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca kaccid arthāś ca kalpante dharme ca ramate manaḥ sukhāni cānubhūyante manaś ca na vihanyate
english: Nārada said: Do your enterprises prosper? Does your mind delight in dharma? Do you experience pleasures, and is your mind not afflicted?

sanskrit: kaccid ācaritāṃ pūrvair naradeva pitāmahaiḥ vartase vṛttim akṣīṇāṃ dharmārthasahitāṃ nṛṣu
english: O lord of men, do you follow the inexhaustible way of conduct practiced by your forefathers and grandfathers — a way accompanied by both dharma and material welfare — among your people?

sanskrit: kaccid arthena vā dharmaṃ dharmeṇārtham athāpi vā ubhau vā prītisāreṇa na kāmena prabādhase
english: Do you not harm dharma by means of material interest, or material interest by means of dharma, or both of them by means of selfish desire, treating affection as paramount?

sanskrit: kaccid arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca jayatāṃ vara vibhajya kāle kālajña sadā varada sevase
english: O best of the victorious, O giver of boons, knowing the proper time, do you always attend to material welfare, dharma, and desire by apportioning them in due season?

sanskrit: kaccid rājaguṇaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saptopāyāṃs tathānagha balābalaṃ tathā samyak caturdaśa parīkṣase
english: O sinless one, do you properly examine the six royal qualities, the seven means of policy, and likewise the fourteen factors of strength and weakness?

sanskrit: kaccid ātmānam anvīkṣya parāṃś ca jayatāṃ vara tathā saṃdhāya karmāṇi aṣṭau bhārata sevase
english: O best of victors, O Bhārata, examining yourself and your opponents, and thus resolving upon actions, do you pursue the eight methods of statecraft?

sanskrit: kaccit prakṛtayaḥ ṣaṭ te na luptā bharatarṣabha āḍhyās tathāvyasaninaḥ svanuraktāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, have your six constituent elements not become diminished — are they prosperous, free from vice, and completely devoted to you?

sanskrit: kaccin na tarkair dūtair vā ye cāpy apariśaṅkitāḥ tvatto vā tava vāmātyair bhidyate jātu mantritam
english: Is your counsel never disclosed through inferences, through envoys, or through those who seem above suspicion — whether it leaks from you or from your ministers?

sanskrit: kaccit saṃdhiṃ yathākālaṃ vigrahaṃ copasevase kaccid vṛttim udāsīne madhyame cānuvartase
english: Do you pursue peace and war at the proper time? Do you follow the right conduct toward the neutral and the mediating power?

sanskrit: kaccid ātmasamā buddhyā śucayo jīvitakṣamāḥ kulīnāś cānuraktāś ca kṛtās te vīra mantriṇaḥ
english: O hero, have you appointed as your ministers men who are your equals in intellect, pure, able to sustain their lives, of noble birth, and devoted to you?

sanskrit: vijayo mantramūlo hi rājñāṃ bhavati bhārata susaṃvṛto mantradhanair amātyaiḥ śāstrakovidaiḥ
english: For victory of kings, O Bhārata, is rooted in counsel, well concealed by ministers rich in counsel and versed in the scriptures.

sanskrit: kaccin nidrāvaśaṃ naiṣi kaccit kāle vibudhyase kaccic cāpararātreṣu cintayasy artham arthavit
english: Do you not fall under the power of sleep? Do you wake at the proper time? O knower of purpose, do you also reflect on your aims in the latter part of the night?

sanskrit: kaccin mantrayase naikaḥ kaccin na bahubhiḥ saha kaccit te mantrito mantro na rāṣṭram anudhāvati
english: Do you not deliberate alone? Do you also not deliberate with too many? Does the counsel you have deliberated upon not run abroad through the kingdom?

sanskrit: kaccid arthān viniścitya laghumūlān mahodayān kṣipram ārabhase kartuṃ na vighnayasi tādṛśān
english: Having determined upon purposes that are small in their beginnings but great in their fruits, do you quickly set about to accomplish them and not obstruct such plans?

sanskrit: kaccin na sarve karmāntāḥ parokṣās te viśaṅkitāḥ sarve vā punar utsṛṣṭāḥ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ hy atra kāraṇam
english: Are not all your affairs out of sight and in doubt, or all of them abandoned? For a mixed approach is the cause of success here.

sanskrit: kaccid rājan kṛtāny eva kṛtaprāyāṇi vā punaḥ vidus te vīra karmāṇi nānavāptāni kāni cit
english: O king, O hero, do your men know which tasks have been accomplished and which are nearly complete, and are there none remaining unaccomplished?

sanskrit: kaccit kāraṇikāḥ sarve sarvaśāstreṣu kovidāḥ kārayanti kumārāṃś ca yodhamukhyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Are all your administrators, versed in all the scriptures, training the princes and the leading warriors in every way?

sanskrit: kaccit sahasrair mūrkhāṇām ekaṃ krīṇāsi paṇḍitam paṇḍito hy arthakṛcchreṣu kuryān niḥśreyasaṃ param
english: Do you purchase one learned man at the price of a thousand fools? For a learned man can bring about the highest good in times of difficulty in one's affairs.

sanskrit: kaccid durgāṇi sarvāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakaiḥ yantraiś ca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurdharaiḥ
english: Are all your fortresses fully stocked with wealth, grain, weapons, water, engines of war, craftsmen, and archers?

sanskrit: eko 'py amātyo medhāvī śūro dānto vicakṣaṇaḥ rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā prāpayen mahatīṃ śriyam
english: Even one intelligent, heroic, self-restrained, and discerning minister can bring a king or a prince to great prosperity.

sanskrit: kaccid aṣṭādaśānyeṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca tribhis tribhir avijñātair vetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ
english: Do you, through three sets of three spies unknown to one another, keep track of the eighteen key positions in the enemy's camp, and the fifteen in your own, using your scouts?

sanskrit: kaccid dviṣām aviditaḥ pratiyattaś ca sarvadā nityayukto ripūn sarvān vīkṣase ripusūdana
english: O destroyer of enemies, unknown to your foes and always prepared, do you constantly and vigilantly watch all your enemies?

sanskrit: kaccid vinayasaṃpannaḥ kulaputro bahuśrutaḥ anasūyur anupraṣṭā satkṛtas te purohitaḥ
english: Is your royal priest a man of good conduct, of noble birth, widely learned, free from envy, not given to questioning others, and honored by you?

sanskrit: kaccid agniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimān ṛjuḥ hutaṃ ca hoṣyamāṇaṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā
english: Is the one appointed over your sacred fires a man who knows the rites, is intelligent, upright, and who always duly reports what has been offered and what is about to be offered at the proper time?

sanskrit: kaccid aṅgeṣu niṣṇāto jyotiṣāṃ pratipādakaḥ utpāteṣu ca sarveṣu daivajñaḥ kuśalas tava
english: Is your astrologer well-versed in the auxiliary branches of the Vedas, expert in astronomy, and skilled in interpreting all kinds of portents?

sanskrit: kaccin mukhyā mahatsv eva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ jaghanyāś ca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ
english: Are the principal servants employed in principal tasks, the middling in middling tasks, and the lowest in the lowest tasks?

sanskrit: amātyān upadhātītān pitṛpaitāmahāñ śucīn śreṣṭhāñ śreṣṭheṣu kaccit tvaṃ niyojayasi karmasu
english: Do you appoint in the highest tasks ministers who have been tested by the fourfold test, whose loyalty was also that of their fathers and grandfathers, who are pure and excellent?

sanskrit: kaccin nogreṇa daṇḍena bhṛśam udvejitaprajāḥ rāṣṭraṃ tavānuśāsanti mantriṇo bharatarṣabha
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, do your ministers not govern the kingdom in such a way that the subjects are greatly troubled by excessively harsh punishment?

sanskrit: kaccit tvāṃ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitaṃ yathā ugrapratigrahītāraṃ kāmayānam iva striyaḥ
english: Do the officiating priests not disregard you as they would a fallen man, or as women disregard one who is excessively demanding in receiving gifts and is driven by desire?

sanskrit: kaccid dhṛṣṭaś ca śūraś ca matimān dhṛtimāñ śuciḥ kulīnaś cānuraktaś ca dakṣaḥ senāpatis tava
english: Is your commander of the army bold, heroic, intelligent, steadfast, pure, of noble birth, devoted to you, and capable?

sanskrit: kaccid balasya te mukhyāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntās tvayā satkṛtya mānitāḥ
english: Are all the chiefs of your army skilled in warfare, of proven valor, brave, and honored and respected by you?

sanskrit: kaccid balasya bhaktaṃ ca vetanaṃ ca yathocitam saṃprāptakālaṃ dātavyaṃ dadāsi na vikarṣasi
english: Do you give the food and wages of the army, which are due at the proper time, as fitting, without delay?

sanskrit: kālātikramaṇād dhy ete bhaktavetanayor bhṛtāḥ bhartuḥ kupyanti daurgatyāt so 'narthaḥ sumahān smṛtaḥ
english: For when food and wages are overdue, retainers become angry with their master on account of their hardship; that is said to be a very great misfortune.

sanskrit: kaccit sarve 'nuraktās tvāṃ kulaputrāḥ pradhānataḥ kaccit prāṇāṃs tavārtheṣu saṃtyajanti sadā yudhi
english: Are all the noble sons of good families principally devoted to you? Do they constantly sacrifice their lives for your cause in battle?

sanskrit: kaccin naiko bahūn arthān sarvaśaḥ sāṃparāyikān anuśāssi yathākāmaṃ kāmātmā śāsanātigaḥ
english: Does not one person, overcome by desire, transgressing your authority, govern all the many affairs leading to the next world just as he pleases?

sanskrit: kaccit puruṣakāreṇa puruṣaḥ karma śobhayan labhate mānam adhikaṃ bhūyo vā bhaktavetanam
english: Does a man who adorns his work through his personal effort receive greater honor or additional food and wages?

sanskrit: kaccid vidyāvinītāṃś ca narāñ jñānaviśāradān yathārhaṃ guṇataś caiva dānenābhyavapadyase
english: Do you honor with gifts, according to their merit and their virtues, men who are trained in learning and skilled in knowledge?

sanskrit: kaccid dārān manuṣyāṇāṃ tavārthe mṛtyum eyuṣām vyasanaṃ cābhyupetānāṃ bibharṣi bharatarṣabha
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, do you support the wives of men who have met death in your cause and those who have fallen into misfortune?

sanskrit: kaccid bhayād upanataṃ klībaṃ vā ripum āgatam yuddhe vā vijitaṃ pārtha putravat parirakṣasi
english: O Pārtha, do you protect like a son an enemy who has submitted out of fear, or who has come unarmed, or who has been defeated in battle?

sanskrit: kaccit tvam eva sarvasyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ pṛthivīpate samaś ca nābhiśaṅkyaś ca yathā mātā yathā pitā
english: O lord of the earth, are you equitable toward all the earth and beyond suspicion, like a mother and like a father?

sanskrit: kaccid vyasaninaṃ śatruṃ niśamya bharatarṣabha abhiyāsi javenaiva samīkṣya trividhaṃ balam
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, when you hear that an enemy is in difficulty, do you attack him swiftly after examining the three kinds of strength?

sanskrit: pārṣṇimūlaṃ ca vijñāya vyavasāyaṃ parājayam balasya ca mahārāja dattvā vetanam agrataḥ
english: O great king, having ascertained the rear guard, the determination of the enemy, and the strength of the army, and having paid wages in advance —

sanskrit: kaccic ca balamukhyebhyaḥ pararāṣṭre paraṃtapa upacchannāni ratnāni prayacchasi yathārhataḥ
english: O scorcher of enemies, do you present to the chiefs of the enemy's army, in secret within their kingdom, gifts of jewels as each deserves?

sanskrit: kaccid ātmānam evāgre vijitya vijitendriyaḥ parāñ jigīṣase pārtha pramattān ajitendriyān
english: O Pārtha, having first conquered yourself and mastered your senses, do you seek to conquer your enemies — those who are negligent and have not mastered their senses?
